questions.questionText: In a certain operation, 12 ⊗ 11 = 120, 11 ⊗ 2 = 11, 8 ⊗ 6 = 40. Using the same rule, what is 11 ⊗ 6 ?
questions.explanation: Test on the first example: 12 ⊗ 11 = 120 fits a×b − a (a = 12, b = 11). The same rule also gives 11 and 40 for the other two. So a ⊗ b = a×b − a, and 11 ⊗ 6 = 55.
questions.shortcut: Try 'a×b' and 'a²' type combinations on the first pair, then confirm on the other pairs.
